what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Read every article again, bottom-up, and predict the shape
sections.para: The newsroom's 187 article graphs barely touch: 48 labels are shared, 401 of 672 tags used once. The owner asks for a second reading of every article as facts, names and sources under one grammar, the layers above left to emerge. This is the brief and ten predictions, published before the run; the article that followed scores them.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Islands today; one grammar, a join, layers that emerge
sections.para: The graphs do not touch. Every article will be read as claims anchored to quotes, names and concepts with one id across the newsroom. Gravity, clusters and peaks are computed from the join and scored against the editor's layers. Ten predictions are made first, and the same text is the standing brief.

sections.label: The memo, and what it asks for
sections.line: Bottom-up graphs, emergent dimensions, peaks, drawn, two articles
sections.para: The owner's memo of 18 October asks for a graph per article from the bottom up, dimensions allowed to appear where the ontology changes, peaks as natural places of arrival, drawings including rUv's hemispheres, and two articles: the brief with predictions first, the comparison after.

sections.label: Where the graphs stand today
sections.line: 2,348 nodes, 48 shared labels, 401 tags used once
sections.para: 187 graphs hold 2,348 nodes and 2,381 edges in eight relations without inverses. 48 of 2,286 labels appear in more than one article. The editor's 44 controlled subjects leave 379 raw tags unmapped. 753 outside citations across 258 domains carry no date. Two earlier readings covered five articles.

sections.label: The grammar that does not change
sections.line: Five rules fixed; types and verbs free per layer
sections.para: Every edge is a verb with a named inverse, the generic association edge is banned, properties carry data not meaning, supersede never delete, render the answer to a question. Each layer chooses its own types and verbs, and the build calls a layer a new dimension only where they change.

sections.label: The file beside every article
sections.line: Claims, edges, names, concepts, sources, dates, validated
sections.para: One JSON file per article holds claims with kind, section anchor and a verbatim quote, edges between claims, names and concepts from seeded registries of 137 and 75, dated sources and dates. The validator refuses a quote not found in the twin. The worked example has 25 claims and passes.

sections.label: How the run goes
sections.line: Brief first, readers in batches, merge, deterministic derivation
sections.para: This article is published before any second reading. Then readers take the articles in batches of about ten with the brief and the validator, new ids are folded into the registries, and code derives the join, gravity, clusters, peaks and pages the same way every time. The second article follows.

sections.label: What a dimension is, and how one is allowed to appear
sections.line: A dimension has its own types and verbs
sections.para: Claims are one dimension, names another, sources and time perhaps more. A count such as gravity or a cluster is a query within a dimension, not a new one, unless describing it needs new words. The editor's topics, desks, series and sections are the control the clusters are scored against.

sections.label: Peaks, hemispheres and the shapes to draw
sections.line: Peaks by gravity and bridging; five drawings to attempt
sections.para: A peak is a node many articles share that also bridges clusters. The drawings: the two-way cut into lobes after rUv's map, a three-dimensional turn on a canvas with no library, the altitude diagram, the peaks as a ridge, and the births of concepts on a date axis, all from the same JSON.

sections.label: Ten predictions
sections.line: Ten numbered predictions, each with its score
sections.para: 3,500 to 5,500 claims; 300 or more shared ids; five dimensions plus one unlisted; six to nine clusters with agents and policy splitting; a control and record cut with the control side larger; named peaks; concept births mostly before October's second week; 1,000 to 1,400 sources; desks mostly holding; and three ways it will go wrong.

sections.label: The standing brief
sections.line: The README beside the files is the brief for every run
sections.para: The same brief lives in the repository as admin/content/graphs/README.md with the validator and derivation in fsg.py, run on every release. Later runs add their expectations to it, say when a layer is stable, and name the articles that moved a cluster.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Nothing read yet; counts by label; hemispheres from memory
sections.para: Every number is the baseline and every claim about emergence a prediction. Counts are by label and tag, not by idea. The hemispheres picture rests on the owner's memory of rUv's map. The readers are the same model as the writer, the registries are seeds, and this is one run of the couple the memo expects.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The owner's memo, the counting script, graphs.sgit.ai's grammar
sections.para: A voice memo of Dinis Cruz on 18 October 2026; counts by fsg.py over articles/graphs.json, find.json and the twins; the grammar from graphs.sgit.ai and the fractal graphs article; the earlier readings and the gravity rule from three articles; the worked example, the README and the validator in the repository.
